To determine if two energy levels can be clearly resolved, their energy difference must be larger than the energy uncertainties (linewidths) arising from their finite lifetimes. According to the energy-time uncertainty principle, the energy uncertainty \(\Delta E\) is related to the lifetime \(\tau\) by \(\Delta E \approx \hbar / \tau\).

Given:
- \(\tau_1 = 10^{-9} \, \text{s}\)
- \(\tau_2 = 10^{-8} \, \text{s}\)
- \(\hbar \approx 6.58 \times 10^{-16} \, \text{eV·s}\)

Calculations:
- \(\Delta E_1 = \hbar / \tau_1 \approx 6.58 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{eV}\)
- \(\Delta E_2 = \hbar / \tau_2 \approx 6.58 \times 10^{-8} \, \text{eV}\)

To clearly distinguish the two levels, their energy separation \(\Delta E\) must be greater than the sum of their widths (or at least greater than the larger width). The sum is on the order of \(10^{-6} \, \text{eV}\). Among the given options, only \(10^{-4} \, \text{eV}\) is significantly larger than this uncertainty. The other options (\(10^{-8}, 10^{-9}, 10^{-11} \, \text{eV}\)) are smaller than the linewidths and would not allow the levels to be resolved.

Answer: B
